AAPL.rationale: Apple's fundamental health is strong: Q2 FY2026 delivered record March-quarter revenue of $111.2B (+17% YoY) and EPS of $2.01 (+22% YoY), with Services hitting an all-time high of $31B (+16% YoY) at 76.7% gross margin. The installed base of 2.35B+ active devices creates a durable recurring-revenue flywheel. Balance sheet is fortress-like with $147B liquidity, $62B net cash, and a new $100B buyback authorization. However, the trajectory has a seasonal QoQ decline (revenue -22.7%, EPS -29.2% from the holiday quarter), and the TTM picture is incomplete due to fiscal calendar gaps, so I cannot confirm a clean trailing trend. Valuation is mid-range vs own history: P/E of 36.6 sits in the middle of the 30.2-43.1 range over the past year, not cheap but not stretched. The stock has rallied +15.3% over the past quarter to $305, which has already captured much of the strong Q2 print. Near-term catalysts are modest: the Q3 guidance of 14-17% revenue growth is solid, and the leadership transition to John Ternus appears orderly, but no single dated catalyst stands out as a clear re-rating event. Risks include rising memory costs pressuring gross margins (47.5-48.5% guided for Q3 vs 49.3% in Q2), ongoing EU DMA regulatory headwinds on the App Store, and elevated 10Y Treasury yields at 4.57% which compress growth multiples. Overall, this is a high-quality franchise with good but not exceptional near-term upside at current levels.
